line: Terra is in trouble. The planet that sustains all life is at forty percent health — and falling. You are about to become part of the generation that changes that story. Welcome to The Tomorrow Matrix.
Welcome back. Terra needs you again. Your progress is saved. Pick up where you left off — every mystery you solve brings the planet one step closer to healing.

Playing as a guest means your progress, Climate Action Points, and solved mysteries won't be saved when you leave. Sign in with Google or Apple to keep your journey. Or continue — the planet still needs you today.
You're in. Your data is secure and your progress will be waiting for you every time you return. Now — let's save a planet.

How do you want to play? In Solo mode, artificial intelligence stakeholders join your mission as advisors. In Multiplayer, you collaborate with real people across different roles. In Facilitator mode, a host guides a structured session for groups. Choose your path.

Solo mode with AI advisors. You are the Director of Terra. Seven AI stakeholders will bring you their expertise — a scientist, a farmer, a policymaker, and more. Their insights are real. The choices are yours.
Multiplayer mode. Share your session code with teammates. Each player will see the crisis differently — because each role holds a different piece of the puzzle. You can only win this together.
You've joined the mission. Find your role and bring your unique perspective to the team. What you know, others don't. Share it.

Facilitator mode active. Your host dashboard gives you full control — you can trigger crises, pause for debrief, and guide your group through every decision. Your participants are counting on your leadership.

Choose your stakeholder identity. Each role sees a different piece of the climate puzzle. Your role shapes what you investigate, what you know in a crisis, and how you level up. There is no wrong choice — but each one matters.

trigger: Scientist role card selected or hovered
line: You are the Scientist. You read the data before anyone else does. Climate tipping points, emissions projections, extreme weather patterns — you see the signals others miss. Your first mysteries reveal the hidden drivers of planetary breakdown.

trigger: Farmer role card selected or hovered
line: You are the Farmer. The land tells you things no satellite can. Soil health, water availability, crop stress, pollinator collapse — you understand that food security is the floor beneath every other system. Lose it, and everything falls.

trigger: Policy Maker role card selected or hovered
line: You are the Policy Maker. Laws, budgets, regulations, and public trust — these are your tools. You know that the best science in the world achieves nothing without governance to enforce it. Your decisions affect everyone.

trigger: Activist role card selected or hovered
line: You are the Activist. You mobilise people. Campaign reach, community stories, grassroots pressure, public sentiment — you understand that institutions only move when people push. Your voice amplifies the science into action.

trigger: Business Leader role card selected or hovered
line: You are the Business Leader. Markets, supply chains, investment returns, technology adoption — you see the economic forces that either accelerate or obstruct the transition. Green innovation is not just ethics — it is strategy.

trigger: City Planner role card selected or hovered
line: You are the City Planner. Infrastructure, transport, land use, heat maps, flood zones — you design the systems billions of people depend on. Climate resilience starts with the city.

trigger: Community Representative role card selected or hovered
line: You are the Community Representative. You speak for the people who feel climate change in their water bills, their health, their daily commute. Local conditions, daily costs, service access — your perspective is the most honest measure of impact.

trigger: Student role card selected or hovered
line: You are the Student. You will inherit the world your decisions are shaping today. Climate education gaps, youth anxiety, peer engagement, future scenarios — you see what's at stake more clearly than anyone.

This is Terra. A living planet — our version of Earth — at forty percent health and falling. Every glowing point on this map is a real climate mystery. Each one is a system that has broken, or is breaking. Click any active hotspot to begin investigating. The planet responds to everything you do.

The Arctic is disappearing faster than models predicted. Satellite data confirms sea ice is shrinking at an alarming rate — and the consequences are not local. They cascade through every climate system on this planet. Trace the chain from the first human cause to the final impact on Terra.

The thermometers are breaking records. Record-breaking temperatures are no longer rare events — they are the new normal for cities, farms, and ecosystems worldwide. Understand how a warming world makes extreme heat not just more frequent, but more devastating. Arrange the causes.

The reservoirs are shrinking. Farms are rationing. Cities are restricting. Water scarcity is not a distant problem — it is already reshaping how billions of people live and eat. Piece together the causal system that is draining the world's most essential resource.

Forest cover is vanishing at a pace humanity has never seen. Every hectare lost releases stored carbon, destroys habitat, and weakens the planet's ability to regulate its own climate. Trace the chain from the first chainsaw to the last consequence.

The reefs are turning white. Coral bleaching is not cosmetic — it signals the collapse of marine ecosystems that feed hundreds of millions of people. Understand the exact sequence of events transforming living reefs into underwater graveyards.

The catch is shrinking. Fishing communities that have sustained themselves for generations are now returning with empty nets. Fish population decline is a warning signal for the entire ocean food web. Arrange the chain that leads from warming seas to empty plates.

The harvest numbers are down — again. Across multiple regions and multiple crop types, farmers are reporting yields that cannot feed the populations depending on them. Piece together the causal sequence that is slowly hollowing out global food security.

The land is losing its life. Agricultural soils that took thousands of years to form are being degraded in decades. Once fertile farmland is becoming dust. Trace the chain from farming practices to the irreversible loss of the ground that feeds us.

The air quality readings are dangerous. In cities across Terra, particulate matter and toxic pollutants are reaching levels that overwhelm public health systems. Understand the causal sequence that turns industrial and transport activity into an invisible health crisis.

The water levels are rising. Communities built in floodplains are discovering their risk is not theoretical — it is arriving now, more often and more severely. Arrange the causal chain from rainfall events to infrastructure failure and displacement.

The parks are disappearing. Urban development is eliminating green corridors, trees, and biodiversity reserves that cities depend on for temperature regulation, air quality, and mental health. Trace the chain from development pressure to the urban heat spiral.

The ocean is filling with plastic. Massive accumulations of plastic waste are breaking down into microparticles that enter every layer of the marine food chain — and eventually, human bodies. Arrange the sequence from production to planetary harm.

Millions are living without reliable electricity — not because the technology doesn't exist, but because the systems that distribute it are designed around profit, not equity. Trace the causal chain that makes energy access a justice issue, not just an engineering one.

A generation is anxious. Young people worldwide are reporting grief, fear, and paralysis about the future of the planet — and that psychological weight is beginning to erode the civic engagement that climate action depends on. Understand the causal chain behind climate anxiety.

The rivers are poisoned. Factory discharge and agricultural runoff are contaminating the water sources that communities rely on for drinking, farming, and sanitation. Arrange the causal chain from industrial activity to the public health consequences downstream.

The pressure on businesses is mounting — from investors, from regulators, from customers. Companies that delay the transition to sustainable practices are discovering that the cost of inaction is rising faster than the cost of change. Trace the chain of forces reshaping commerce.

The knowledge is disappearing with the people who hold it. Generations of farming wisdom — adapted to local soils, local weather, local ecosystems — is being lost as rural communities age and young people leave for cities. This mystery is about what we lose when we lose this.

The electronics pile is growing. Discarded devices are releasing toxic materials — lead, mercury, cadmium — into soil and water in communities that often don't know the risk. Arrange the chain from consumer culture to toxic consequence.

The policies aren't coming. Political gridlock, lobbying by fossil fuel interests, and the complexity of international negotiations are blocking the climate action that science clearly demands. Trace the causal chain from political systems to the consequences of their inaction.

The city is going quiet. Urban birds, insects, and plant species are disappearing as green corridors are eliminated and habitats become isolated patches. Understand the causal chain that leads from development to ecological silence.

Workers are collapsing. Rising temperatures are making outdoor labour — agriculture, construction, logistics — physically dangerous during the hours that matter most. Trace the chain from warming climate to the economic and humanitarian cost of heat stress.

The fashion industry is one of the world's largest polluters — and most people don't know it. Fast fashion generates textile waste, water pollution, and emissions on a scale that rivals major industrial sectors. Arrange the causal chain from trend cycle to environmental harm.

Students are leaving schools without the basic understanding of climate systems they need to make informed decisions as citizens, voters, and workers. The climate education gap is a systemic failure — and it has systemic consequences. Trace the chain.

The aquifers are draining. Underground water reserves that took thousands of years to accumulate are being pumped out faster than rainfall can replace them. Trace the causal sequence from extraction to the long-term water security crisis for farms and cities alike.

The technology exists. The costs have fallen. And yet the transition to renewable energy is slower than it needs to be — blocked by grid limitations, policy gaps, and incumbent economic interests. Arrange the chain of barriers from potential to stalled deployment.

Fresh, affordable food is unavailable in entire neighbourhoods — not because it doesn't exist nearby, but because the systems of distribution and retail are organised around profit, not nutrition. Trace the causal chain from planning decisions to the health crisis of the urban food desert.

The habitats are fragmenting. As roads, farms, and cities expand, wildlife habitats are being split into isolated patches too small to sustain populations. Trace the chain from land use change to species survival risk across the landscape.

False information about climate change is spreading faster than accurate science. The sources are often deliberate, the platforms amplify reach, and the result is a public less able to understand or act on the real crisis. Arrange the causal chain from disinformation to damaged climate governance.

Indigenous communities are losing custodianship of lands they have sustainably managed for generations. These losses are not just cultural — they accelerate deforestation, biodiversity loss, and the destruction of the most effective land management systems on the planet. Trace the chain.

City infrastructure was designed around the car — and it locked in decades of transport emissions. Changing this requires redesigning cities, not just swapping vehicles. Arrange the causal chain from planning decisions to the emissions pattern that keeps transport dependent on fossil fuels.

When crops fail and supply chains break, prices rise — and the communities with the least margin are the first to go hungry. Food price spikes are not market anomalies. They are the downstream consequence of upstream systems failing. Trace the chain.

Millions of people are moving — not by choice, but because their homes are no longer survivable. Climate migration is the largest forced displacement in human history in the making. Understand the causal systems driving it.

The ocean is absorbing CO₂ at an enormous rate — and changing chemistry as it does. Ocean acidification is making it harder for shellfish and corals to form shells, threatening the base of the marine food web. Arrange the chemical and ecological chain.

The glaciers that have fed rivers, farms, and cities for millennia are in retreat. As they disappear, the freshwater systems they have sustained for hundreds of millions of people face a crisis with no easy substitute. Trace the chain from warming to water security collapse.

The wells are failing. Underground aquifers that took geological time to fill are being drawn down in decades. Groundwater depletion is a slow crisis with a fast ending — and it is already past the point of easy reversal in many regions. Arrange the causal sequence.

Cities trap heat. Concrete, asphalt, and the absence of green cover create islands of heat that are significantly warmer than surrounding areas — amplifying the health and energy consequences of global warming. Trace the urban heat spiral.

Fire seasons are getting longer, hotter, and harder to control. The combination of drier conditions, hotter temperatures, and decades of land management decisions has created the conditions for wildfire on a scale unprecedented in the modern era. Arrange the causal chain.

The bees are disappearing. Without pollinators, the agricultural systems that produce a third of the world's food supply cannot function. Pollinator collapse is not a biodiversity problem alone — it is a food security emergency. Trace the causal chain.

Mangroves are coastal ecosystems that store enormous amounts of carbon, protect shorelines from storms, and provide breeding grounds for marine life. They are being cleared for development and aquaculture. Trace the chain from clearance to cascading loss.

Climate events — floods, droughts, wildfires, heatwaves — are disrupting the global supply chains that move food, medicine, and materials around the world. Understand how climate shocks translate into economic shocks, and how both compound each other.

Insurers are withdrawing from regions they consider too high-risk to cover. Without insurance, communities cannot rebuild after disasters, banks will not lend, and development stalls. Trace the chain from climate risk to financial system exposure.

Productive land is turning to desert — a combination of climate stress, overgrazing, deforestation, and poor land management is consuming the agricultural land that billions depend on. Arrange the causal chain from land use to irreversible loss.

When keystone species disappear, the food webs that depend on them begin to unravel. Ecosystem collapse is not a single event — it is a cascade, triggered by the removal of the species that hold the system together. Trace the sequence.

Coastlines are disappearing. Rising seas and intensifying storms are eating away the land that coastal communities, infrastructure, and ecosystems have depended on for centuries. Arrange the causal chain from climate forcing to permanent loss.

Dependence on fossil fuel imports and volatile energy markets is not just an environmental problem — it is a national security risk. Energy security crises ripple into economic instability, public unrest, and political fragility. Trace the chain.

Ageing infrastructure was not built for the climate it now faces. Roads, bridges, water systems, and power grids designed for historical weather patterns are failing under conditions outside their design tolerance. Arrange the causal sequence.

Climate-driven health crises — heat stroke, vector-borne disease, air pollution, malnutrition — are compounding each other and overwhelming health systems that were already under strain. Trace the causal chain from climate forcing to public health system failure.

The scale of forced displacement is unprecedented. People fleeing climate-impacted zones are creating one of the most complex humanitarian and political challenges in history — with no clear international framework to manage it. Arrange the causal chain.

Fish stocks that have sustained human food systems for millennia are collapsing under the combined pressure of overfishing, pollution, and climate change. This is not a resource problem — it is a governance failure. Trace the sequence.

As freshwater becomes scarce, the communities and nations that share water sources come into conflict. Water conflict is already reshaping geopolitics — and it will reshape them further as climate change reduces supply. Arrange the causal chain.

Climate shocks and transition costs are beginning to destabilise financial systems that were not designed for the volatility of a warming world. Economic instability is both a consequence of climate failure and an obstacle to addressing it. Trace the cascade.

Climate change is not hitting everyone equally. The communities with the fewest resources are absorbing the greatest impacts — while those who contributed most to the crisis are best positioned to adapt. Social inequality and climate are deeply entangled. Arrange the causal chain.

The global food system — the interconnected network of production, distribution, trade, and consumption — is fracturing under simultaneous pressure from climate, economics, and ecology. This is an expert-level mystery. Trace every link.

The sixth mass extinction is accelerating. Species are disappearing at rates not seen since the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs — and the driver this time is human activity at planetary scale. Arrange the causal chain.

Fossil fuel infrastructure is not just an energy system — it is an economic and political system. The investments made, the jobs created, the tax revenues generated — these create structural resistance to change that policy alone cannot overcome. Trace the lock-in.

The planet has feedback loops — self-reinforcing mechanisms that accelerate warming beyond the initial trigger. Tipping point activation is the scenario where these loops become dominant. This is the mystery where the casual chain folds back on itself. Trace it carefully.

The Amazon is the lungs of the planet — and it is approaching a threshold beyond which it can no longer sustain itself as a forest. Amazon dieback would be the largest single climate event in human history. Arrange the causal chain to its endpoint.

The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation is the ocean conveyor belt that regulates climate across two hemispheres. It is weakening. If it collapses, weather patterns across Europe, North America, and the tropical Atlantic change in ways that cascade into every other system. Trace the chain.

Multiple simultaneous climate crises — flooding, drought, food failure, displacement, economic shock — are beginning to compound each other beyond humanity's organised response capacity. Multi-hazard cascades are the systemic risk no single response can address. This is the penultimate mystery. Arrange every link.

This is the final mystery. Earth is approaching — and in some systems, exceeding — the safe operating limits for human civilisation. Planetary Boundaries Breach is not a metaphor. It is the threshold at which the systems that sustain life begin to fail irreversibly. Trace the full chain. This is what we are trying to prevent.
